newsitem.title: USA: Merck surges, earnings lift US drug group.
newsitem.headline: Merck surges, earnings lift US drug group.

text.p: Surging Merck & Co shares led the U.S. drug group higher Thursday afternoon, on the heels of its announcement earlier in the day of slightly higher than expected second quarter earnings.

Analysts said the Merck results calmed the drug-sector after a downturn Wednesday prompted by Pfizer Inc's announcement late Tuesday of second quarter results that fell a bit short of Wall Street expectations.
Merck was up eight to 106-1/2, with almost five million shares changing hands.
It lifted the boats of Warner-Lambert Co, up 7/8 to 139-7/8; Johnson & Johnson, up one to 63; Pfizer, up 1-1/8 to 60-3/8; and Eli Lilly Co, up 1/2 to 114.

Merck had reported earnings per share of $0.96 for the second quarter, one cent above the First Call consensus estimate and an increase of twenty percent over net earnings seen in the same 1996 quarter.
It had reported 20-percent worldwide sales growth to $5.9 billion for the second quarter, fueled by stronger sales of blockbuster anticholesterol drug Zocor and other key products.
"It was a great quarter for Merck," said Gruntal & Co pharmaceuticals analyst Adam Greene.

Greene said he was impressed Zocor's worldwide sales jumped 25 percent to $865 million in the quarter despite stiff competition from Lipitor, the potent cholesterol fighter launched in February by Warner-Lambert.
"Merck alleviated concerns that Lipitor was seriously attacking its franchise in the cholesterol market. That didn't happen because the whole market has expanded," Greene said.

Lipitor, being co-marketed with Pfizer, in recent weeks has captured over 20 percent market share of new prescriptions for anti-cholesterol drugs -- including Zocor and Bristol-Myers Squibb Co's Pravachol.
Greene said while Lipitor has chipped away at Zocor's market share, it will likely actually help competitors by increasing overall demand for the so-called "statin" drugs.
Other Merck drugs also showed impressive sales growth, analysts said, including osteoporosis drug Fosamax, whose year-on-year sales jumped 92 percent to $127 million.

Sales of the New Jersey company's ulcer drug Pepcid rose 27 percent in the second quarter to $285 million. And sales of antihypertension drugs Cozaar and Hyzaar, which are sold together, leaped 101 percent to $161 million.
But sales of Mevacor, another Merck cholesterol-lowering drug, slumped 11 percent in the second quarter to $285 million.
Although a majority of analysts Thursday said they were impressed with Merck's second quarter results, Salomon Brothers analyst Robert Uhl expressed surprise at the Merck rally.
"Merck's results were slightly better than expected but I'm mystified why it is up so much. I didn't find anything that was particularly positively surprising" in the earnings report, he said.
Uhl said part of Merck's earnings gain was attributable to a lowering of its tax rate in the second quarter from 30.3 percent to 29.3 percent.
